transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-11 16:00 PT | Duration 54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Dr. Elena Park, Marcus Lee, Sara Nguyen, Omar Khalid.

Summary (auto): High-level ops playbook handoff for pilot: network topology (VPC vs on-prem), data residency / HIPAA questions, pilot scope (2 weeks), benchmarking plan, and next steps. Action items assigned.

Topics: playbook walkthrough, security constraints, pilot telemetry, SLA expectations, model selection & cost tradeoffs.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Marcus (Northridge): yep loud and clear, thanks.
[00:10] Maya: great. quick intros, i'm Maya, i'm the AE here working with Northridge, Jonah's our solutions engineer and will run the bench and Priya is your CS lead.
[00:20] Dr. Elena Park: thanks, i'm Elena VP Eng, leading the integration for our clinical-doc summarization flow.
[00:25] Sara: sara, head of ai, i'll own model validation and evals.
[00:28] Marcus: marcus, s re team, i'll do networking and infra.
[00:31] Omar: omar, infosec - HIPAA/compliance and regs.
[00:34] Maya: perfect. goal for today: handoff the ops/playbook for the pilot, align on network choices (hosted vs private), security requirements, define bench and success criteria, and confirm next steps.

[03:05] Jonah: i'll start with the pilot architecture slide, we propose a two-week pilot using Redwood Dedicated in us-west and a private routing path for PHI — right now we have two options: hosted but with customer VPC peering, or bring-your-own on-prem agent. there are tradeoffs re latency and cost.
[03:28] Marcus: peering sounds promising but we have to confirm egress rules, don't want outbound to the public internet for PHI.
[03:33] Omar: yes we need to be strict: encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, key separation — can Redwood integrate with our Azure KeyVault?
[03:42] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys via common KMS providers, we also have an HSM option for Private deployments. we'll attach the KMS integration doc afterwards. Link: https://redwood.example/sec/northridge-kickoff-pack.pdf

[05:10] Jonah: quick note on model variants: for the summarization workload we recommend testing a smaller 13B quantized variant for cost-sensitive paths (lower token costs, slightly higher latency) and a 70B float/quant for high-quality fallback. Redwood allows pinning model versions and automatic fallback based on latency SLOs.
[05:34] Sara: what's the observed quality delta? we need F1 and clinical accuracy metrics, not just perplexity.
[05:40] Jonah: yeah, we'll run the eval suite you send; we expect small drops on entity recall for the 13B but often acceptable with prompt engineering and retrieval augmentation. we'll produce per-prompt quality breakdowns.

[07:12] Dr. Elena Park: timeline question: we have a compliance window end of month, want pilot done before that. is two-week pilot realistic?
[07:21] Maya: yes two weeks for pilot is typical; Jonah's mini-bench first week, integration + smoke tests second week.
[07:27] Marcus: for networking, we prefer VPC peering with strict egress rules. can Redwood provide static egress IPs and a list of ports?
[07:36] Priya: yes we'll share the network workbook and static IP ranges. that is in the runbook link we'll send after.

[09:00] Omar: audit logs — we need user-level traceability and retention policies for six years per our compliance team, can Redwood export audit logs to our SIEM?
[09:09] Jonah: we have streaming audit logs to customer endpoints (S3, GCS, or syslog) and also built-in per-request traces in the console. retention config is flexible.
[09:20] Omar: ok, send format examples.

[11:48] Maya: let's run through the ops playbook: onboarding checklist, credential management, model pinning, canary route config, fallback hierarchy, and runbook for incident triage.
[11:58] Marcus: incident triage — do you have runbooks for KV cache corruption or tokenization mismatches? we've had weird tk-b tokenization issues in other LLM infra.
[12:08] Jonah: yes we have KB articles. KV (k v) cache is handled at the runtime with eviction policies; if there is mismatch we can flush caches per-deployment. i'll note down that tokenization mismatch doc.

[14:30] Sara: on telemetry — we need token-level cost and latency broken down per-route and per model. will Redwood give us pre-built dashboards and also raw telemetry?
[14:40] Priya: yes both; console includes per-route latency histograms, and we'll enable a dumps pipeline to your datalake if you want raw events.
[14:48] Marcus: does that include per-token breakdowns so we can calculate unit economics?
[14:52] Jonah: yep, token-level breakdowns plus recommended batching configurations to meet your cost targets.

[17:22] Dr. Elena Park: security question again — data residency: some records must stay in-region and cannot cross to another jurisdiction. can we constrain models and routing to region-specific pools?
[17:33] Maya: absolutely, we support region pinning and routing policies so requests never leave the specified region or VPC. for on-prem you control everything.

[19:00] Omar: SSO and RBAC — we want SCIM + SAML SSO and fine-grained role controls. is SCIM provisioning supported?
[19:08] Priya: yes, SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO are supported; RBAC roles can be mapped to groups and you can limit per-route model access.

[21:15] Jonah: now a bit on performance expectations: for the 13B quantized model we expect p50 token latency around 40–60 ms on our dedicated a100-style pools with batching tuned; for the 70B it's closer to 120–180 ms depending on seq length. we'll capture your seq distribution to tune batching and kernels.
[21:45] Marcus: what about KV cache effectiveness with our use case? repeated context across patient messages could benefit.
[21:52] Jonah: yes prefix caching should give you big gains; if many requests share lookup prefixes, requests will hit cached KV pages and reduce per-token compute. we'll show cache hit projections in the benchmark.

[24:05] Dr. Elena Park: can we do warm-up runs on real-ish data to estimate cold-start behavior? we don't want initial latency spikes.
[24:14] Jonah: we can simulate warm cache conditions as part of the bench; we'll also provide guidance on pre-warming and keeping warmed sessions with sticky routing.

[26:45] Sara: regarding evals — we'll provide 200 canonical docs and scoring rubric; how do you run regression alerts?
[26:54] Priya: Redwood Optimize can monitor prompt sets and raise alerts when quality drifts beyond thresholds. we can wire up your scoring signals to the alert system.

[29:10] Maya: procurement note: typical pilot pricing, usage caps and overage, and then conversion to dedicated reserved capacity if you choose to commit. i'll send a pilot pricing worksheet.
[29:22] Dr. Elena Park: do you do usage-based discounts during pilot?
[29:26] Maya: we can provide credits for pilot usage and reasonable pilot discounts; we'll include that in the estimate.

[32:00] Marcus: can Redwood support an air-gapped or on-prem container if needed?
[32:08] Jonah: yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments; there are additional support and licensing terms; performance profile is slightly different due to hardware variance but we can provide guidance.

[34:30] Omar: legal — we need a data processing agreement (DPA) and BCAs if patient data crosses regions; do you have standard DPA templates?
[34:40] Maya: yes we'll share our DPA and SOC2 reports; if there are special clauses we'll ask legal to review.

[36:50] Priya: runbook excerpt: first 72 hours checklist, DNS & firewall checklist, SAML test plan, telemetry pipeline test, and rollback instructions. any questions on the playbook?
[37:05] Marcus: rollback — how do you rollback a canary that has model regressions at scale?
[37:11] Jonah: rollback is model pin + route swap. we support instantaneous route-level fallback to a pinned model or warm earlier snapshot. plus automatic detection rules can flip to fallback on error rate or latency spikes.

[39:20] Sara: curious about evals in closed loop — can we push labels back to retrain or is that out of scope for Redwood?
[39:28] Maya: Redwood focuses on serving and inference lifecycle; we can integrate with your training pipelines and export logs/labels but we don't host training pipelines directly.

[41:50] Dr. Elena Park: ok let's align success criteria for the pilot: 1) <150ms p95 for the high-quality route for seq length ~512, 2) entity recall >= 92% on the eval set, 3) secure end-to-end with KMS and SSO, 4) stable telemetry with dashboard.
[42:10] Maya: good set — Jonah will produce bench results, Priya will set up dashboards and retention, and i'll share pricing and contract.

[44:00] Jonah: i'll scope the bench: we'll run the 200 evals, 3 model variants, measure p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit simulation, and cost per 1k tokens. deliverable: bench report and follow-up call.

[46:30] Omar: one more on encryption at rest jurisdiction — some PHI cannot leave CA datacenters. can you guarantee data residency for logs and backups?
[46:40] Maya: we can enforce region-only storage for backups and provide attestations. details in the security packet.

[49:10] Priya: sample artifacts to share: onboarding runbook (doc), network workbook (spreadsheet), mini-bench script & prompt list, SOC2 + HIPAA mapping doc. we'll drop links in the recap.

[51:00] Dr. Elena Park: sounds good. any blockers?
[51:05] Marcus: network approvals — need IP ranges and firewall change window.
[51:10] Omar: legal to review DPA but no blockers otherwise.

[52:00] Maya: recap: Redwood sends security packet + runbook + pricing sheet; Jonah runs bench and delivers report by 3/18; schedule security deep-dive for 3/17 at 10am PT; Priya will create console access for two test users.
[52:20] Dr. Elena Park: agreed.
[53:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[53:10] Meeting end.
